h1:
Where to Stay in Tak?
10 Hotels We Actually Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites!
heroSub: 10 hand-picked Tak hotels across every budget — a riverside hotel on the Ping River in Tak town, boutique and budget stays in border-town Mae Sot, and a riverside resort that serves as a base for the Thee Lor Su waterfall in Umphang. Covering Tak town, Mae Sot and Umphang. From roughly ฿450–1,300/night.
introH2: 🏞️ Why does choosing the right area in Tak matter so much?
introHtml: Tak is a large province with sights scattered across very different corners — its stays fall into three areas that take a real drive to get between. Tak town sits on the Ping River, with the Trok Ban Chin walking street, town markets and a position on the northern route, ideal for a one-night stopover or arriving without a car. Mae Sot district is about 80 km from Tak town over the Phawo mountain pass — a border town next to Myanmar with the Rim Moei market, Shan temples and the widest choice of stays. And Umphang district is the furthest out, around 160 km on from Mae Sot along a famous 1,219-curve road, the base for the Thee Lor Su waterfall and whitewater rafting. Many people book without checking the area and end up driving across districts all day. This guide rounds up 10 hand-picked Tak hotels across every tier — all with real guest reviews, prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Tak has no train line and no metro — you get around mainly by car, with a small Mae Sot airport (some domestic flights) and a small Tak airport. Pick your area by your itinerary: Tak town is on the Ping River, near the Trok Ban Chin walking street, markets and the road up to Bhumibol Dam, best for a stopover; Mae Sot is the border town near the Rim Moei market, the Mae Sot crossing and Shan temples, with the most stays — both boutique and budget — making it the natural base for the border area; and Umphang is the base for the Thee Lor Su waterfall and rafting on the Mae Klong, where most resorts bundle a stay with a tour. The distances between Tak town, Mae Sot and Umphang are long and mountainous, so allow plenty of driving time. Almost every hotel has free parking, so they suit self-drivers well.

entries.name: Viang Tak Riverside Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chom Phon Rd · on the Ping River · central Tak
tags: 🚶 Near Trok Ban Chin walking street
entries.addr: 236 Chom Phon Rd, Rahaeng, Mueang Tak
entries.storyHtml: Viang Tak is the most-reviewed hotel in this guide by a wide margin — 1,595 reviews, scoring 8.7. It's a riverside hotel on the Ping River in the heart of Tak town that travellers on the northern route have stopped at for years. Its standout is the Deluxe River View room, with big windows looking onto the Ping River and the Somphot Krung Rattanakosin bridge, plus a location within walking distance of the Trok Ban Chin walking street. It's a fit for a town-centre stopover where you want a hotel with plenty of review data behind it.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For the full feel, take a Deluxe River View — the Ping River outlook is worth the few hundred baht over a town-view room.
pros: Most reviewed in this guide at 1,595 — solid data
River View rooms look onto the Ping River and bridge
Central Tak-town location, walk to Trok Ban Chin
Ideal for a stopover on the northern route, with parking
cons: An older, long-established hotel — the River View rooms are fresher than some others
Town-view rooms are cheaper but miss the river, so check the room type first

entries.name: Hop Inn Mae Sot
tags: 🛣️ On the Asian Highway, easy to reach
entries.addr: 81/9 Asian Highway, Mae Sot, Mae Sot District
entries.storyHtml: Hop Inn Mae Sot is the hotel with the highest score in this guide — 9.2. It's a Hop Inn budget-chain hotel selling simplicity done consistently clean across every branch: fresh rooms with air-con, a TV, a fridge and hot water, from ฿700, plus free parking. It sits on the Asian Highway in Mae Sot, easy to drive in and out of — a fit for self-drivers exploring the border area who just want a reliably comfortable room.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Hop Inn is usually cheaper booked ahead online than as a walk-in; take the rate with breakfast included if you'd rather not hunt for a morning spot.
pros: Highest score in this guide at 9.2
Fresh, clean rooms to a consistent chain standard
From ฿700 with free parking
On the Asian Highway, easy to drive in and out
cons: A budget stay — plain rooms, no pool or extra facilities
On a main road outside the market area, so you drive into Mae Sot town

entries.name: The Teak Hotel
tags: 🎨 Warm timber-toned design, fresh and clean
entries.addr: 888 Prasat Withi Rd, Mae Sot, Mae Sot District
entries.storyHtml: The Teak Hotel is a new boutique hotel in Mae Sot town scoring a high 9.1. Its draw is the warm timber-toned styling and a fresh, clean feel; the Deluxe rooms run about 30 sqm and the Deluxe Corner is a corner room with good light. It sits on Prasat Withi Road in town, handy for the market and restaurants — a fit for anyone wanting a stylish room at a price that's still easy on the wallet.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The step up from Superior to Deluxe is small in price but clearly bigger in space — worth it for a multi-night stay.
pros: High 9.1 score for a new boutique in Mae Sot
Attractive timber-toned design, fresh and clean rooms
Spacious ~30 sqm Deluxe rooms, good for several nights
In Mae Sot town, handy for the market and restaurants
cons: Fewer reviews than the long-established town hotels
No swimming pool — the focus is on the room design

entries.name: Centara Life Hotel Mae Sot
entries.addr: 100 Inthakhiri Rd Soi 5 (Asian Highway), Mae Sot District
entries.storyHtml: Centara Life is the top-tier hotel in this guide — a Centara-group 4-star with a swimming pool, scoring 8.4 from 436 reviews. It's the pick for anyone wanting a big-chain standard in Mae Sot: rooms run about 25–26 sqm, with Junior and Executive Suites for families or longer stays. It sits on the Asian Highway and has a pool, which is rare in Mae Sot — a fit for business travellers or anyone who wants the full set of facilities.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as a group or staying several nights? Look at the 36 sqm Junior Suite — split between you the per-person cost drops, and you gain a sitting area.
pros: Centara-group 4-star, the top tier in this guide
Has a swimming pool — rare in Mae Sot
Suites with spacious rooms, good for families and longer stays
Big-chain standard, a fit for business travel
cons: The Booking score sits at 7.8, noticeably below the Agoda side
On the Asian Highway outside the market area, so you drive into town

entries.name: B2 Mae Sot Boutique & Budget Hotel
entries.addr: 365 Moo 10, Mae Pa, Mae Sot District
entries.storyHtml: B2 Mae Sot is the cheapest hotel in this guide, from just ฿550, and well reviewed at 407 reviews, scoring 8.7. It's a B2-chain budget hotel selling clean rooms at a light price in the Mae Pa area on the edge of Mae Sot, ranging from a ฿550 Superior up to a ฿900 Deluxe Triple for three people or a small family. It's a fit for budget travellers self-driving the border area who just need a clean room at a friendly price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as three, take the ฿900 Deluxe Triple — split between you it's far cheaper than booking two double rooms.
pros: Cheapest hotel in this guide, from ฿550
Well reviewed at 407 — solid data for a budget stay
Clean rooms to the B2-chain standard
Has a Deluxe Triple for three, with parking
cons: In the Mae Pa area on the edge of town, so you drive into Mae Sot
A budget stay — plain rooms with no extra facilities

entries.name: Irawadee Resort
entries.addr: 758 Inthakhiri Rd, Mae Sot, Mae Sot District
entries.storyHtml: Irawadee Resort is a small Lanna-Burmese-style boutique resort in central Mae Sot, scoring 8.7 from 310 reviews. Its draw is the timber decor that blends Lanna and Burmese art to suit the border-town setting, with small balconies on the rooms and breakfast included. It sits on Inthakhiri Road in Mae Sot town, easy to get around from — a fit for anyone who'd rather have a stay with character that matches the border feel than a plain hotel.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The VIP Room is the most fully decked out in Lanna-Burmese style — if you want the full resort feel, the few hundred baht extra is worth it.
pros: Distinctive Lanna-Burmese decor that suits the border town
Good-feeling small resort, breakfast included in every room
310 reviews, with an Agoda score as high as 9.1
Central Mae Sot location, easy to get around
cons: A small resort with limited rooms — fills fast on long weekends
The entry Deluxe is noticeably smaller than the Superior/VIP rooms

entries.name: White House Hotel Tak
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mai Ngam · Mueang Tak · ~3 km from the town centre
entries.storyHtml: White House Hotel is a hotel with a swimming pool on the Tak-town side, well reviewed at 532 reviews, scoring 8.6. Its draw is the pool and a Family Room, ideal for parents who want the kids to be able to swim. It's in Mai Ngam, about 3 km from the Tak town centre, with parking and clean rooms with hot water — a fit for families passing through Tak who want a stay with a pool at a friendly price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling with kids, take a pool-view Standard King or the Family Room — easy access to the pool for only a little more than a standard room.
pros: Has a swimming pool, ideal for families with kids
Well reviewed at 532 — solid data
Has a Family Room for larger groups
From ฿850 with parking

entries.name: Thee Lor Su Riverside Resort
entries.revCount: Agoda 9.0 · Booking 9.0 · Thee Lor Su base
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On the Mae Klong River · Umphang
tags: 🏞️ Base for the Thee Lor Su waterfall
🍳 Meals and a guide on offer
entries.storyHtml: Thee Lor Su Riverside is a resort on the Mae Klong River that serves as a popular base for the Thee Lor Su waterfall, scoring 9.0. Its draw is the riverside setting in Umphang and the packages that bundle the stay with meals, rafting and a guided trek to the Thee Lor Su / Pitugro waterfalls all in one place. Rooms range from a ฿1,000 standard cottage to a riverside house with a terrace over the stream — a fit for anyone set on visiting Thee Lor Su who wants the resort to arrange the tour.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If Thee Lor Su is the goal, contact the resort about a stay-plus-tour package ahead of time; in high season (Nov–Feb) it's busy and you need a national-park quota slot.
pros: On the Mae Klong River, a good base for Thee Lor Su
Bundles stay + meals + rafting + trekking in one package
Scores 9.0 on both Agoda and Booking
Has a riverside house with a terrace over the stream
cons: In Umphang, about 160 km from Mae Sot on a winding road — allow plenty of driving time

entries.name: Umphangburi Resort
entries.badge: 🏞️ Riverside · near the Thee Lor Su trailhead
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Umphang · near Thee Lor Su
tags: 🚣 Near the Thee Lor Su trailhead
entries.storyHtml: Umphangburi Resort is a riverside resort in central Umphang, near the Thee Lor Su trailhead, scoring 8.3. Its draw is the central-Umphang location, which makes onward trips easier than from a resort outside town; it has wooden riverside cottages and the owner can arrange Thee Lor Su / rafting tour packages. It has rooms for three for larger groups, making it another solid base for anyone exploring Umphang who wants to stay in the centre of town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask the owner about a stay-plus-Thee Lor Su tour package ahead of time — it's arranged more completely and conveniently than sorting a separate tour yourself.
pros: Riverside in central Umphang, easy for onward trips
Near the Thee Lor Su trailhead and the rafting put-in
Has rooms for three, good for larger groups
The owner can arrange tour packages
cons: In Umphang, a long way from Mae Sot on a winding road — allow plenty of driving time
Fewer reviews (62), and the starting price is higher than its Umphang peers

entries.name: Silayok Grand Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mahat Thai Bamrung Rd · Rahaeng · Tak town
entries.addr: 315/18 Mahat Thai Bamrung Rd, Rahaeng, Mueang Tak
entries.storyHtml: Silayok Grand is the cheapest in-town hotel in this guide, from just ฿400–450, scoring 8.1 from 161 reviews. Its draw is the location on Mahat Thai Bamrung Road in Tak town, easy to get around from, at a very light price for an in-town hotel. Rooms have air-con, a flat-screen TV, a fridge and hot water, ranging from a ฿400 Standard up to a ฿690 larger Deluxe — a fit for stopover travellers or anyone on a budget who just wants a cheap in-town room.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The ฿400 Standard is fine for a single night, but for several nights or two people the larger Deluxe is more comfortable for only a little more.

faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about Tak hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in in Tak?
faq.a: It depends on what you've come to see. Tak town suits a stopover on the northern route — on the Ping River, near the Trok Ban Chin walking street (Viang Tak, White House, Silayok). Mae Sot is the border town with the most stays, a base for the Rim Moei market and the Mae Sot crossing (Hop Inn, The Teak, Centara Life, B2, Irawadee). Umphang suits anyone set on the Thee Lor Su waterfall and rafting (Thee Lor Su, Umphangburi). The areas are far apart on mountainous roads, so allow plenty of driving time.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Tak hotels cost?
faq.a: Tak is fairly affordable: budget and in-town hotels start around ฿400–700 a night (Silayok, B2, Hop Inn); boutiques and 3-star hotels are around ฿800–1,000 (Viang Tak, The Teak, Irawadee, White House); and the 4-star with a pool plus the Umphang-side resorts run around ฿1,000–1,300 (Centara Life, Thee Lor Su, Umphangburi). In the Thee Lor Su high season, Umphang-side prices and room availability are tighter than usual.

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay to visit the Thee Lor Su waterfall?
faq.a: If you're set on the Thee Lor Su waterfall, stay on the Umphang side, near the trailhead and the rafting put-in. Thee Lor Su Riverside Resort ฿1,000 sits on the Mae Klong River and bundles stay + meals + tour. Umphangburi Resort ฿1,300 is riverside in central Umphang, where the owner can arrange tours. Umphang is about 160 km from Mae Sot on a 1,219-curve road, so allow plenty of driving time and book a national-park quota slot ahead.

faq.q: ❓ Which Tak hotels have a swimming pool?
faq.a: In this guide, the ones with a pool are Centara Life Hotel Mae Sot (a Centara-group 4-star on the Mae Sot side) and White House Hotel (a pool and a Family Room on the Tak-town side, about 3 km from the centre). Both suit families who want the kids to be able to swim, from ฿850–1,200.

faq.q: ❓ Where's the best place to stay in Mae Sot?
faq.a: Mae Sot is the border town with the widest choice of stays in Tak. For the highest score, take Hop Inn Mae Sot 9.2 at ฿700. For a stylish boutique room, take The Teak Hotel 9.1 at ฿900 or Irawadee Resort in Lanna-Burmese style. For a 4-star with a pool, take Centara Life ฿1,200. On a budget, take B2 Mae Sot ฿550, the cheapest.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Tak hotel?
faq.a: On ordinary weekdays, booking 1–2 weeks ahead is plenty, as Tak isn't a crowded market. But on the Umphang side in the Thee Lor Su high season (November–February) and on long weekends, stays and tour slots fill fast, so book and arrange your national-park quota 2–4 weeks ahead or more.
